text.p: Australian Anthony Painter admitted his good fortune after firing a third-round 68 for a two-shot lead in the Coolum Classic golf tournament on Saturday.
Painter's eventful round gave him an aggregate 207, nine under par and two shots clear of overnight leader and compatriot Rod Pampling.
Painter said he was lucky to escape punishment for some poor shots during his round, which ended on a favourable note when he chipped in from off the green for a birdie at the 18th hole.
"I must have been the luckiest player on the course. My bad shots were terrible and my good shots were great," Painter said.
Pampling battled bravely all day for a one-over 73 to stand alone on seven under par.
New Zealander Michael Long was alone in third place on six under par after a third-round 71.
